questions.text: Can the business meet its financial obligations over the period ahead from money it holds or reliably expects?

A.text: Near-term obligations cannot reliably be met; payments are being delayed or deferred out of necessity

B.text: Obligations are being met, but with no buffer — an unexpected cost or a delayed receipt would create a shortfall

C.text: Obligations can be met over a defined forward period, with a modest buffer for ordinary variation

D.text: Obligations can be met over an extended forward period, with a buffer sized to withstand a realistic adverse event — a lost major customer, a delayed payment, a cost increase

E.text: As D, and the coverage position is monitored on a defined cycle, so deterioration would be identified well before it became urgent

questions.text: After all the costs of running the business — not only the direct costs of delivery — does the business generate a surplus?

A.text: Not known; total costs are not tracked well enough to say

B.text: Costs are known and the business operates at a deficit, with no defined path to surplus

C.text: Operates at a deficit, but the path to surplus is defined with specific evidenced assumptions — which costs, which volumes, by when

D.text: Generates a surplus, or has reached the point where it does so under normal operating conditions

E.text: Generates a surplus consistently, and the business understands which parts of it generate or consume that surplus

questions.text: How does the business manage the timing of money coming in and going out?

A.text: Timing is not managed; shortfalls are discovered when they occur

B.text: Timing is tracked informally; occasional shortfalls are handled reactively as they arise

C.text: Expected receipts and payments are tracked forward over a defined horizon, so shortfalls can be anticipated

D.text: As C, and the business actively manages the drivers — collection terms, payment terms, and money tied up in stock or work in progress — rather than only observing them

E.text: As D, as a routine discipline with evidence it works: shortfalls are anticipated and addressed before they affect obligations or operations

questions.text: How current and reliable is the financial information available to whoever makes decisions?

A.text: Records are incomplete or so out of date that the current position is unknown

B.text: Records exist but are compiled infrequently, or only for tax and compliance, so decisions are made without current figures

C.text: Records are maintained on a regular cycle and give a reliable picture of the current position

D.text: As C, and the information is broken down enough to show where money is earned and spent — by offering, customer type, activity, or location

E.text: As D, and the figures are reviewed on a defined cycle by whoever makes decisions, with discrepancies investigated rather than absorbed

questions.text: Does the business plan its financial position forward?

B.text: Rough expectations exist but are not written down or worked through

C.text: A forward plan exists, built on stated assumptions, covering a defined period

D.text: As C, and actual results are compared against the plan, with variances understood rather than noted

E.text: As D, and the plan is revised based on what those comparisons reveal, with alternative scenarios considered for the uncertainties that would matter most

questions.text: What is the weight of the business's fixed financial commitments — loans, leases, and other ongoing obligations — relative to what it generates?

A.text: Commitments are not fully known, or are at a level the business is struggling to service

B.text: Commitments are known and being serviced, but consume enough that little remains for anything else

C.text: Commitments are known and comfortably serviced — or the business deliberately carries none — and their terms are understood

D.text: As C, and commitments are deliberately chosen and structured as to terms, timing and security, rather than accumulated as circumstances required

E.text: As D, and the business has tested that it could continue meeting them under a realistic downside
